The mouse is covered. This step lets players bop with Q W E, A S D, and Z X C, start a round with Space, stop it with Escape, and press Enter in the name box. It also deals with the surprises keyboards bring: held keys, capital letters, and keys typed into text boxes.

## Listen for keys

Two events cover most keyboard work:

- `keydown` fires when a key goes down, and keeps firing while it's held.
- `keyup` fires once, when the key is released.

Key events go to the element that has **focus**: the text box you're typing in, the button you tabbed to, or the page itself when nothing else is focused. Like clicks, they bubble up, so a listener on `document` hears keys pressed anywhere on the page. That's the usual place for game controls.

<Playground>
```html
<p id="last">Click here, then press any key.</p>
```
```js
const last = document.querySelector("#last");

document.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  last.textContent = `You pressed ${event.key}`;
  console.log(event.key, event.code);
});
```
</Playground>

The preview is its own small page, so click inside it before pressing keys. Otherwise your key presses go to this lesson page instead.

## Look inside a key event

The lab below shows the two most useful properties for every key you press. Click the dashed box first, then try letters, Shift + 1, the arrow keys, Space, and holding a key down.

<EventLab kind="keyboard" />

## key or code?

- `event.key` is what the key means right now: the character it types, or a name like `"Enter"`.
- `event.code` is which physical key was pressed, named by its position on a standard US keyboard.

| You press | `event.key` | `event.code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `"a"` | `"KeyA"` |
| Shift + A | `"A"` | `"KeyA"` |
| 1 | `"1"` | `"Digit1"` |
| Shift + 1 | `"!"` | `"Digit1"` |
| Space bar | `" "` | `"Space"` |
| Enter | `"Enter"` | `"Enter"` |
| Esc | `"Escape"` | `"Escape"` |
| Up arrow | `"ArrowUp"` | `"ArrowUp"` |

Use `key` for most shortcuts: letters, Enter, Escape, arrows. Use `code` when the position matters more than the character. Space is a good example: `event.code === "Space"` reads more clearly than comparing to a string with one space in it.

Watch out for capital letters. With Shift or Caps Lock on, pressing Q gives `"Q"`. Calling `event.key.toLowerCase()` handles both.

<Predict question="A player holds Shift and presses the 1 key. What is event.key?" options={['"1"', '"!"', '"Digit1"']} answer={1}>
With Shift held, the 1 key types `!`, so `event.key` is `"!"`. `event.code` is still `"Digit1"`, because it names the physical key.
</Predict>

## Held keys repeat

Hold a key down, and after a short pause the keyboard starts repeating it. Each repeat fires another `keydown`, with `event.repeat` set to `true`:

<Playground>
```html
<p>Click here, then hold down any key for a second.</p>
<p id="counts">keydown: 0 · repeats: 0 · keyup: 0</p>
```
```js
const counts = document.querySelector("#counts");
let downs = 0;
let repeats = 0;
let ups = 0;

function show() {
  counts.textContent = `keydown: ${downs} · repeats: ${repeats} · keyup: ${ups}`;
}

document.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  downs += 1;
  if (event.repeat) {
    repeats += 1;
  }
  show();
});

document.addEventListener("keyup", () => {
  ups += 1;
  show();
});
```
</Playground>

In a game, a held key shouldn't count as twenty bops. Ignoring events where `event.repeat` is `true` keeps one press to one action.

## Modifier keys

Shift, Control, Alt (Option on a Mac), and the Windows or Command key are **modifiers**. Every key event says which ones were held: `event.shiftKey`, `event.ctrlKey`, `event.altKey`, and `event.metaKey`.

<Playground>
```html
<p>Click here, then press Ctrl + S (or Command + S on a Mac).</p>
```
```js
document.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  const saving = (event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === "s";
  if (saving) {
    event.preventDefault();
    console.log("Saved! (Pretend we saved something.)");
  }
});
```
</Playground>

`preventDefault()` stops the browser from opening its own Save dialog. Only take over a familiar shortcut when your page really does that job.

## Stop the browser's default action

Some keys have built-in jobs. Space and the arrow keys scroll the page, and Enter submits forms. If your listener handles one of these keys, call `event.preventDefault()` so the page doesn't also scroll. Leave every other key alone, or typing elsewhere on the page will break.

Move the 🙂 by 20 pixels for each arrow key press: right and down add to `x` and `y`, left and up subtract. Update `player.style.left` and `player.style.top`, and call `preventDefault()` for arrow keys only. Click the preview before testing with **Run**.

## Which element hears the key?

Typing in a text box fires `keydown` on the box first, and then the event bubbles up to `document`. So a listener on `document` also hears everything typed into forms:

<Playground>
```html
<input id="note" placeholder="Type here, then click outside and type again" />
```
```css
#note { width: 100%; max-width: 360px; padding: 6px 8px; }
```
```js
const note = document.querySelector("#note");

document.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  if (event.target === note) {
    console.log(`Typed into the box: ${event.key}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`Shortcut key: ${event.key}`);
  }
});
```
</Playground>

`event.target` tells you where the key went. Game shortcuts should skip keys typed into form fields; otherwise, pressing Space in the name box would start a round instead of typing a space.

## Practice: add keyboard shortcuts to a search box

<Exercise id="search-box">
Many sites let you press `/` to jump to the search box. Build that, plus two keys inside the box:

- **Enter** shows `Searching for "QUERY"…` in `feedback`, with the query trimmed. If the box is empty, show `Type something first.`
- **Escape** clears the box and the message.
- **/** anywhere else on the page moves focus into the box with `search.focus()`. Typing `/` inside the box should still work normally.
</Exercise>

## Apply it to the game

### Add a hint

Add a line under the message in `workshop/index.html`, so players know the keys:

```html title="In workshop/index.html, after the message"
      <p id="message" class="message" role="status"></p>
      <p class="hint">Bop with your mouse or the key shown in each hole. Space starts. Escape stops.</p>
```

### Find a hole by its key

Each hole stores its key in `data-key`. Add a function after `hideBot` that searches the holes for a key, using a loop and an early return:

```js title="Add after hideBot in workshop/script.js"
function findHole(key) {
  for (const hole of holes) {
    if (hole.dataset.key === key) {
      return hole;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

It returns `null` for any key that isn't on the board, like Shift or `p`.

### Enter in the name box

At the end of the file, listen for Enter on the name box itself:

```js title="Add at the end of workshop/script.js"
// Enter in the name box starts the round.
nameInput.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  if (event.key === "Enter") {
    startGame();
  }
});
```

### Keys for the whole page

Then add one listener on `document` for everything else:

```js title="Add at the end of workshop/script.js"
document.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  // Keys typed into the form belong to the form, not the game.
  if (event.target === nameInput || event.target === speedSelect) {
    return;
  }
  // Holding a key repeats keydown. One press should mean one bop.
  if (event.repeat) {
    return;
  }

  if (event.code === "Space") {
    event.preventDefault();
    startGame();
  } else if (event.key === "Escape") {
    endGame();
  } else {
    const hole = findHole(event.key.toLowerCase());
    if (hole !== null) {
      bop(hole);
    }
  }
});
```

Read it from the top. Keys typed into the form are skipped, and so are repeats. Space starts a round (and `preventDefault()` stops the page from scrolling), Escape ends it, and any other key is looked up on the board. `bop()` already ignores keys pressed between rounds.

There's one more detail working for you. When a round starts, `startGame` disables the controls fieldset. A disabled text box can't keep focus, so focus returns to the page. Without that, after pressing Enter in the name box, every Q, W, or E you pressed would be typed into the box, and the first check would skip it.

## Run and check

| Try this | What should happen |
| --- | --- |
| Press Space with nothing selected | A round starts, and the page doesn't scroll |
| Press the key in MISAbot's hole, in either case | The score goes up |
| Hold a key down over MISAbot | Only one bop counts |
| Press Escape mid-round | The round ends with your result |
| Type `Mary Ann` in the name box | The space types normally, and no round starts |
| Press Enter in the name box | A round starts, and your keys reach the game |
